STEP 1 - Scene: A plated home-style meal (possibly a light dinner) photographed from above at a near-top-down angle. The plate sits on a glass table with a wooden base beneath.

STEP 2 - Ruler: A square white plate, roughly 26 cm across. Its visible width is about 340 px and the plate looks roughly square-ish with slight perspective, so I size it at ~26 cm. Area ≈ 3.14 × (13)² ≈ 530 cm² (treating it as a round-equivalent vessel).

STEP 3 - Items:
- Cherry tomatoes (halved, about 6–7 pieces)
- Green beans (about 12–15 pieces)
- Roasted potatoes with onion and herbs
- Mushrooms (a few, mixed in)
- Baked fish or chicken fillet with herb/vegetable crust (two pieces, one larger)

STEP 4 - Area (percent of plate area):
- Cherry tomatoes: 8% (≈42 cm²)
- Green beans: 9% (≈48 cm²)
- Roasted potatoes with onion/herbs: 17% (≈90 cm²)
- Mushrooms: 3% (≈16 cm²)
- Fish/chicken fillet pieces: 22% (≈117 cm²)
Total food cover ≈ 59% of the plate, which is consistent with a partly filled plate.

STEP 5 - Volume (area × typical height):
- Cherry tomatoes: 42 cm² × 2.5 cm ≈ 105 ml
- Green beans: 48 cm² × 1.5 cm ≈ 72 ml
- Potatoes/onion: 90 cm² × 2.5 cm ≈ 225 ml
- Mushrooms: 16 cm² × 1 cm ≈ 16 ml
- Fish/chicken: 117 cm² × 2 cm ≈ 234 ml

STEP 6 - Grams (× bulk density):
- Cherry tomatoes: 105 × 0.6 ≈ 63 g
- Green beans: 72 × 0.5 ≈ 36 g
- Potatoes/onion: 225 × 0.8 ≈ 180 g (roasted, dense starchy pieces)
- Mushrooms: 16 × 0.5 ≈ 8 g
- Fish/chicken: 234 × 0.95 ≈ 222 g

STEP 7 - Energy (kcal/100 g, as plated):
- Cherry tomatoes: 18 kcal → 63 g ≈ 11 kcal
- Green beans: 31 kcal → 36 g ≈ 11 kcal
- Roasted potatoes with onion: 110 kcal → 180 g ≈ 198 kcal (includes some oil from roasting)
- Mushrooms: 22 kcal → 8 g ≈ 2 kcal
- Baked fish/chicken with crust: 170 kcal → 222 g ≈ 377 kcal

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Total ≈ 509 g and ≈ 599 kcal. For a plate about 60% covered with a protein, potatoes and vegetables, this is plausible, and it falls in the same range as the worked Example B.
